svg.text: Why LLMs Misbehave 🤖💥 · autoregressive dynamics
Same loop as before — but with one brutal twist: there is no backtracking. A single bad token can't be undone,
so it cascades into the failures you actually see in the wild.
⛓️ The root cause: one bad token → cascade (you can't take it back)
Token 1

🌀 Hallucination
🧭 Task drift
🔁 Repetition
🖼️ The failure gallery (every one is "a low-prob token got picked, then snowballed")
🌿 Branching → task drift: "Write a Python function" can start def or import re (both fine) — but if it samples
function (0.1%), it commits to JavaScript and can't switch back.
🔢 Math errors: digits come out one at a time; one wrong digit (9109 vs 9163.78) dooms the rest → use a calculator/code tool.
❄️ Errors snowball: "Is 9677 prime? → No" (wrong) then it fabricates a fake factorization to stay consistent with its own mistake.
🧠 Lack-of-knowledge hallucination: doesn't know a package → invents a "probable" name instead of saying "I don't know".
Famous case: a hallucinated pip install huggingface-cli got 30,000 downloads in 3 months.
📚 Frequent-pattern default: C→F is ×9/5 + 32; change it to ×7/5 + 31 and the model STILL returns the common answer (wrong).
🔁 Repetition loops: self-reinforcing same-token loops — worse on older / smaller models.
🎯 LLMs don't see truth — they see probability. Likely token ≠ correct token.
⚡ What to actually do about it
🛡️ Ground it (RAG) · give it tools (calculator/code for math) · structured outputs · let it reason first (CoT / reasoning models) ·
verify or ensemble · and remember: post-training (RLHF/DPO) tries to make the most-likely token also the most-correct one.
📡 2026 reality check
📦 Slopsquatting is a live supply-chain attack: attackers register hallucinated package names → ship malware. Jan 2026 a fake
npm pkg spread to 237 repos via AI agents. Pkg-hallucination: GPT ~5% vs open-source ~22% → ALWAYS verify AI-suggested packages.
📊 Broad hallucination runs 15–52% across 37 models (2026). Prompt tweaks cut ~22 pts; ensembles catch 30–50%.
⚠️ Some reasoning models hallucinate MORE than older versions — depth ≠ accuracy.
🔑 The structural root is "no backtracking":
it commits one token forever before seeing the consequences. That's exactly why reasoning models "think" in scratch
tokens (revise before committing the answer), and why diffusion LLMs — which CAN revise tokens — are an exciting alternative.
